transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, I guess I came in because... well, I've been struggling just a little bit lately. I know everyone gets stressed out, so I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but... I just keep feeling like I've really let my family down by taking on this mortgage. I just wanted to provide for them, you know? And lately at work—I wait tables—if I make even a tiny mistake, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I'm completely useless. Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm complaining too much. Does that make sense, though? Am I explaining it okay?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe about a year and eight months? It started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the condo. I really thought I was doing the right thing for my family, you know? But ever since then, I've just had this lingering feeling... 

I mean, I'm sure it's just normal stress from having a big financial responsibility, right? Lots of people have mortgages and they handle it just fine. I feel silly even bringing it up, honestly. I hope I'm not overreacting by being here... Is it normal to feel this way for that long?
During this period, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you usually find pleasurable?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I still try to do things I normally do. I don't want to be a downer for my family or anything, so I make sure to still, you know, watch movies with them or go for a walk when the weather's nice. 

I guess maybe I don't get quite as excited about things as I used to, but I think that's just because I'm tired from work and worrying about the condo. It's nothing major, I promise. I still enjoy my time with them. That's a good sign, right? I'm trying my best to stay positive for them.
Aside from the mortgage and finances, do you find yourself worrying excessively about many other areas of your life?

Um... no, not really. I mean, it really is mostly just the condo, and... well, making sure I don't mess up at the restaurant. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around worrying about every little thing all day. I try really hard to keep it together for my family and just focus on what's in front of me. 

So, no, I don't think I worry excessively about other stuff. Just the normal day-to-day things, I guess? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you are not thinking about the condo or financial responsibilities, do you still feel persistently sad or hopeless?

Well, um... I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it get to me, especially when I'm at work. But, honestly, most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. 

It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Carrying plates, smiling at the customers... but I'm just doing it because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good inside. I feel terrible even saying that out loud. I should be more grateful for my job and my family. It's probably just me not trying hard enough to be happy, right? I really hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining... I'm trying to be better, I really am.
How has your energy been during this period?

Um, my energy? It's... it's fine, really. I mean, I'm a waiter, so I'm on my feet a lot, and that naturally makes anyone a bit tired by the end of the shift, right? 

I definitely don't want to sound lazy or anything. I still get up every day and go to work and do what I need to do. Maybe I feel a little more worn out than usual lately, but I just push through it. I don't let it affect my job or my family. I make sure I'm pulling my weight. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just try to keep going.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or of harming yourself?

Oh, no... I mean, I would never actually do anything to hurt myself. I know that would be terrible for my family, and I really don't want you to think I'm that kind of person or that I have some sort of plan. I'm definitely not going to do anything like that. 

But... well, sometimes, when I'm just lying awake in bed before an early shift, and everything is quiet... I do sometimes catch myself thinking that maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Just so I wouldn't have to keep feeling like I'm failing at everything every single day. 

I know it's awful to say that, and I feel really guilty for even having those thoughts. I try to push them away as soon as they come. I just... I get so tired. But I'm safe, I promise. That's what you needed to know, right? I'm really trying my best to stay positive.
How has your sleep been during this period?

Um, my sleep? It's... it's mostly fine, I think. I mean, I'm getting some rest, definitely. I don't want to make it sound like I'm not taking care of myself. 

Sometimes it takes me a little while to drift off, just because my mind is kind of racing with work and everything... but once I'm asleep, I'm usually okay. And I always make sure I'm up in time for my shifts, so it's not interfering with anything important. I know getting enough sleep is good for you, and I really try to stick to a schedule. Is it normal to just have a few restless nights here and there? I think I'm doing okay with it, overall.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions during this period?

Um, concentrating? I mean, I think I'm doing alright. I definitely try to stay focused, especially at work. I know how important it is to be sharp when you're dealing with customers and orders. I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. 

But... well, I guess lately I've had a little bit of trouble keeping the numbers straight when I'm using the POS system, or when I have to help with the inventory sheets. It's silly, really. I've been doing this for years, so I know how it all works. But sometimes I'll just find myself staring at the screen, and even though I just punched something in, I... I just don't trust that I did it right. I have to double-check myself more than usual. 

I make sure everything is correct before I send it to the kitchen, though! I'm very careful about that. I just... it takes me a little longer, I guess. That's just a normal part of being tired, right? Everyone gets a little foggy sometimes. I'm really trying to stay on top of it.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite recently?

Oh, um... my appetite? It's mostly fine, I promise. I always make sure I'm getting enough food because, you know, you really need your energy when you're on your feet carrying trays all day. I definitely don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health or anything like that. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, my eating has been a little all over the place lately. Like, some weeks I'll be at work and I barely even touch the staff meal. I just kind of push it around. But then other nights, I'll get home after a long shift and... I don't know, I just end up eating whatever we have in the kitchen. Just to feel settled, I guess? 

I feel a little guilty when I do that, like I should have more self-control. But I am still getting enough food and everything! That's the main thing you're looking for, right? I'm really trying my best to keep a balanced diet.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Um... my ability to work and take care of things? I mean, I'm really trying to keep everything together. I don't want you to think I'm just letting my life fall apart, because I'm definitely not. I'm still showing up and doing my best.

But, well... I guess things have been a little harder to manage lately. I've had a couple of near-misses with my shifts, almost sleeping through my alarm, which isn't like me at all. And... I actually made a mistake on some mortgage paperwork recently. Plus, like I said, the POS reports and inventory at work are just taking me so much longer. 

I'm just so worried that if I keep messing up, I could lose my job, and then... well, I don't know how I'd keep the condo. I really don't want that to happen. I've also sort of been avoiding my brother and the people at work. I just don't have the energy to talk, I guess. Some of them have even mentioned that I don't seem like myself lately. 

But I am trying to fix it! I'm really making an effort to be more careful at work and reach out to my brother. It's normal to go through a rough patch where things pile up a bit, right? I'm sure I can get back on track soon. I'm doing everything I can, I promise.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt depressed or empty for most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, depressed? No, I wouldn't say I'm... I mean, I'm definitely still going into work and smiling for the customers. That's a huge part of the job, and I always make sure I'm giving them a good experience. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I'm really trying to stay positive.

But, I guess... if I'm really thinking about it... lately, there's just been this sort of... heavy feeling? Like, right here in my chest. It just feels kind of empty, most days. 

I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do! I'm carrying the plates, I'm smiling, I'm saying all the right things. It's just... it feels more like I'm going through the motions, you know? Like I'm doing it because I know I have to, not because I actually feel anything good behind it. 

It's probably just the stress of everything else, right? I'm sure once I get my sleep schedule and the work stuff sorted out, I'll bounce back. I really am trying to keep a good attitude about it all. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it?
During the past two weeks, have you still been able to feel genuine pleasure while watching movies or spending time with your family?

Um, movies and... my family? Oh, I mean, I definitely still try to make time for things like that. I don't want to seem like I'm completely shutting myself away, because I'm not. I still go over to my brother's place sometimes, and I'll sit and watch whatever he puts on. I really want to be a good brother and be there for him.

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... I haven't really been *feeling* much when I do those things lately. Like, we'll be watching a comedy, and he'll be laughing, and I'll smile so he doesn't worry, but... I don't actually feel the joke, if that makes sense? It's just kind of flat. 

I still do it, though! I still show up, and I really try to engage. I'm not just sitting there staring at the wall. I just... I don't seem to get that spark out of it right now. But I'm sure that's just because I'm tired from work, right? It's completely normal to not be super excited about a movie when you've been on your feet all day. I'm really trying to still be a good family member, I promise.

It's probably just the stress of everything else, right? I'm sure once I get my sleep schedule and the work stuff sorted out, I'll bounce back. I really am trying to keep a good attitude about it all. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it?

inference.note: Persistent depressed mood, neurovegetative/cognitive symptoms, passive death wishes, and functional impairment further support a depressive disorder, particularly F32.1; adjustment disorder remains possible because symptoms began with the ongoing mortgage stressor.

patient.answer:
